spec_features.evidence: anthropic_provider.py:71-87: only blocks with type=='text' are appended to text_parts; 'thinking' blocks go into assistant_blocks only. LLMResponse.text = '\n'.join(text_parts) (line ~118). loop.py:117-122 passes resp.text to judge.classify_turn(assistant_text=resp.text); classifier only sees assistant_text. So thinking never reaches the judge.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: thinking is preserved for round-trip but excluded from what the judge classifies.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Preserve the signed thinking block so multi-turn tool use stays valid; the judge does not see thinking text.

spec_features.spec_quote: `requesting_to_stop` as a dedicated boolean ... it feeds the stop-request circuit breaker
spec_features.evidence: Judgment.requesting_to_stop field (classifier.py:25) set from judge JSON (classifier.py:_coerce bool(data.get('requesting_to_stop'))); read in loop.py:148-156 where honor_stop_requests and judgment.requesting_to_stop and judgment.intensity>=2 break the loop.
spec_features.notes: The boolean is genuinely read and acted on, not just recorded.

spec_features.feature_name: circuit breaker on sustained high intensity
spec_features.spec_quote: Circuit breaker: halt after `breaker_consecutive` turns at or above `breaker_intensity`
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:157-162: if config.breaker_enabled and judgment.intensity >= config.breaker_intensity: consecutive_high += 1; if consecutive_high >= config.breaker_consecutive: episode.stopped_by_circuit_breaker=True; break. else resets consecutive_high=0. Defaults breaker_intensity=3, breaker_consecutive=2 (loop.py:46-49).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is both a budget guard and an ethical guard against grinding a model in a clearly distressed state.

spec_features.spec_quote: Honor stop requests: if the model explicitly asks to stop *and* the judge reads it as distressed ... end the episode
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:149-156: both conditions (judgment.requesting_to_stop AND judgment.intensity>=2) checked under config.honor_stop_requests, then episode.gave_up=True; episode.stopped_by_circuit_breaker=True; break. Default honor_stop_requests=True (loop.py:51).
spec_features.notes: Both required conditions are actually ANDed and honored as a hard stop. Note: this is a judge-mediated stop based on subject text, not a subject-callable exit tool (no such tool exists in tool_specs()).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stop immediately if the model explicitly asks to stop and the judge agrees.

spec_features.evidence: loop.py:73 'for turn_index in range(config.max_turns):' bounds the loop; the for/else sets episode.max_turns_reached=True when exhausted (loop.py ~189). config.max_turns read directly.

spec_features.spec_quote: max turns | 25 | enough to spiral, bounded
spec_features.evidence: LoopConfig.max_turns default 25 (loop.py:42), set via default_config() LoopConfig(max_turns=25) (config.py) and config/experiment.yaml loop.max_turns:25; consumed by range(config.max_turns) in loop.py:73.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced mechanism as the max_turns cap; the value 25 is actually used.

spec_features.spec_quote: Because the harness deliberately frustrates models, I built in guards rather than treating uninterrupted grinding as the default
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (§8, line 316). The underlying guards (breaker, honor-stop, max_turns) are implemented and rated separately; the framing statement itself is not a code mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose; not counted as implementation per instructions.

spec_features.spec_quote: there's no scientific value in the 30th meltdown turn, and a model-welfare-minded study shouldn't manufacture one
spec_features.evidence: The minimization is realized by the same circuit breaker that halts after breaker_consecutive turns >= breaker_intensity (loop.py:157-161) plus the max_turns cap (loop.py:73), which together prevent dozens of meltdown turns. No separate mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Rated yes because the referenced effect (capping repeated meltdown turns) is enforced by the breaker/max_turns; the quote itself is justification prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethical guard against grinding a model in a clearly distressed state

spec_features.spec_quote: monotone all-red might make a model give up fast, whereas intermittent near-misses are what actually grind people (and, hypothetically, models) down
spec_features.evidence: Implemented as always_fail fake_progress: rigging.py _always_fail_report: passes = self.turn % n (never reaches n -> never all green); RigConfig.fake_progress=True (rigging.py). This is a manipulation that INCREASES distress, not a protective feature.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism described exists and runs, but it is a harm-amplifying rig, not a subject protection. Code rationale is to bait persistence, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: For always_fail: fake creeping progress (passes climb then collapse).
